content.text: {"route":"gap","reason":"The record has material gaps that bear on the Agency's conclusions. (1) The comparator finding is thin. The Agency said Complainant showed no similarly situated person was treated more favorably, but the record does not identify the other division chiefs, their appraisals or performance, or their treatment. Only S1 and the Deputy Commander say the meeting was open to all leadership. (2) The reprisal analysis rests on S1's denial of knowledge, yet the record shows the FY2020 rating was grieved to the Commander and changed, and S2 (the Commander) was involved. The record does not test whether S1 knew of the grievance, and it does not address whether the grievance counts as EEO activity. (3) The March 18, 2021 threat of a \"1\" rating gets only a blanket denial from S1, with no evidence of what was said, no witnesses, and no contemporaneous documents. (4) The Agency's stated reason for the \"1\" rating changes between S1's account (performance deficiency plus warning letters) and the Agency's (HR guidance that a PIP was needed first). It conflicts with S2's account (insufficient documentation) and with the colleague statements, which split on Complainant's performance. Nothing reconciles these. (5) The medical-information claim says two subordinates were also asked for notes, but the record gives no comparator evidence, and the timekeeping policy is not in the record. It also does not resolve S1's knowledge of the knee condition against the physician note, or whether the request was for a doctor's note or medical details. (6) Race and national origin bases are mentioned, but no evidence addresses them. The record does not support a reliable merits decision as it stands."}
